thread:
alex-support: FYI support case from Acme Analytics — their corporate card keeps declining at charge time. Bank message: 'merchant category restriction (MCC 5734)'. They've tried two corporate cards + one personal backup, all declined. Attached gateway error below.

alex-support: Gateway error (copied from their console):
```
{"error":{"type":"card_error","code":"merchant_blocked","message":"card not allowed for merchant category: 5734","charge_id":"ch_3xYz...","decline_code":"mcc_restricted"}}
```

alex-support: They also mentioned their finance team enforces MCC blocks for subscriptions tied to "analytics services". Customer wants to pay today — asked if we can accept PO or alternate payment method.

jess-billing: Thanks Alex. Do we have the customer's account id / billing profile? Also need the card last4 and brand to log with Stripe/payments partner. If they can provide a PO we can generate an invoice.

alex-support: Account: acct_00912, billing profile id bp_77. Card last4: 4242 (VISA). Charge attempts show the same decline. Customer said their procurement only allows vendors in MCC 5734 explicitly blocked — weird because MCC 5734 is "computer software stores" per some lists.

mike-payments: Noted. Merchant category restrictions are enforced by issuers, so issuing bank is blocking the MCC. We can try: 1) re-route the payment via our payments partner (sometimes different acquirers have different MCC assignment) 2) generate invoice for wire/ACH 3) request sales to accept PO + manual invoice. Which is fastest here?

sasha-sales: If they can sign a PO that's usually fastest for enterprise deals. Do we have PO acceptance configured for acct_00912? Also need to confirm contract terms for delayed payment. I can reach out to the buyer. @jess-billing can you prepare a pro-forma invoice?

jess-billing: I can generate a one-time invoice, but finance requires a signed PO for > $10k. What's the invoice amount?

alex-support: Customer said monthly commit ~$2,200 for a dedicated instance — under the $10k threshold, so billing can accept a PO-less invoice if they prefer card. But they want a PO because of internal policy.

mike-payments: Quick technical ask: can you paste the raw gateway response header? Need acquirer decline code + acquirer message. Sometimes the acquirer declines with code '59' or text 'merchant category not allowed'.

alex-support: Pasted headers: `Acquirer-Response: 305|DECLINED|merchant_category_restricted`. Also `acquirer_code: 305`.

mike-payments: OK that's consistent with issuer-level MCC block. Short-term workaround: we can accept payment by ACH/wire today (jess can provide banking details) or set up invoice via the console and mark it as "due on receipt". Long-term: we can ask payments partner to try reprocessing through alternate acquirer, but that can take 24-72h and requires ops change.

sasha-sales: Customer asked if we can change our merchant descriptor or MCC. Is that possible?

mike-payments: MCC is determined by the merchant account / acquirer. We can't arbitrarily change it per customer — it's global for our merchant account. We could open a request with the acquirer to reclassify, but that usually needs justification and can take weeks. Not a short-term fix.

jess-billing: For now I'll prepare a pro-forma invoice (due on receipt) and wire instructions. I'll cc finance and send to the buyer. If they still insist on card, suggest they request their bank to whitelist our MCC or approve the merchant.

alex-support: I already told them to contact their issuer to whitelist our payments descriptor. They asked if we can supply a 'merchant category code' we use so procurement can whitelist it — what is ours?

mike-payments: Our current MCC is 7399 (Business Services) in the acquirer UI, but the acquirer may surface a different code to issuers (some map to 5734). I'll confirm with the payments provider and report back.

payments-bot: Automated note: raised ticket #PMT-4421 with payments provider (include MCC verification). ETA 48h.

sasha-sales: Great. Alex, tell the customer: (1) we can take ACH/wire immediately, (2) we can send invoice due on receipt, (3) we'll try acquirer reclassification but that takes time. Which option do they prefer?

alex-support: Customer prefers invoice + wire. They're sending a signed PO for records. I'll coordinate. Marking this thread resolved from support POV unless billing/payments need anything else. :white_check_mark:

jess-billing: I'll send invoice now and include wire instructions. Leaving note to finance to accept PO if it arrives.

mike-payments: I'll follow up with payments provider and update ticket. If provider confirms our MCC mapping we can share exact code to customer for whitelist.

alex-support: Thanks everyone. Closing loop — customer paid via wire, confirmed receipt this morning. They also filed a ticket with their bank to whitelist our descriptor. Reopen if payments provider reports reclassification success. :tada:
